Hi Irene,

We're finalizing our DPA annex and need to confirm a few operational details before legal signs off. Two specific asks: 

1) Backups/snapshots: our infosec requires a short, auditable retention window for backups used for restores. Can you confirm Redwood's standard backup purge cadence (how long a full snapshot is retained) and whether you can provide a signed manifest (hash list) proving deletion of snapshots once purged?

2) Logs and diagnostics: we understand application logs are useful for debugging post-incident. Mediconnect needs a possible exception to retain certain diagnostic logs for up to 90 days for half of our production namespaces. Is Redwood able to support a scoped log-retention exception and what governance (change order, SOC evidence, additional cost) would be required?

We're also compiling a short questionnaire (attached) with some optional evidence fields — if you can return the checklist and a proposed cadence by EOD Tuesday that would keep things on schedule.

Thanks,
John

Mediconnect

Irene — thanks for flagging. Operational and legal input below; I'm attaching a subprocessor notification template you can send to Mediconnect if they need more detail about our infra providers.

Snapshots/backups (prod):
- Standard: full snapshot retention is 45 days for production clusters by default.
- Soft hold: we keep a 7-day soft window where snapshots are flagged but not physically purged to allow rapid restore; after 7 days we run the purge workflow.
- Physical deletion proof: we can provide a signed manifest (SHA-256 hashes per snapshot ID) and a purge certificate noting purge date/time and the responsible job/instance. That meets most auditors' requirements.

Logs/diagnostic exception:
- We can accommodate a scoped exception for up to 90 days BUT the customer must accept a formal change order. Requirements:
  - Signed change order (DocuSign) acknowledging scope and retention specifics.
  - Possible incremental charge (tiered by namespace/volume); we'll provide an estimate.
  - Security gating: additional monitoring and quarterly attestation for the exception.

Suggested language to send to Mediconnect (short):
"Redwood's standard backup purge window for production is 45 days with a 7-day soft-hold for recent restores. For audit purposes we can provide a purge manifest (SHA-256 per snapshot) and a purge certificate. Scoped diagnostic log-retention exceptions (up to 90 days) are available by signed change order and are subject to additional fees and quarterly attestation."

I'll also loop in Security for the attestation schedule — Rishi, can you confirm the attestation cadence and what evidence pack we should provide (SOC artifacts + manifest)?

— Kim
Head of Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference

Hi John — thanks for the clear questionnaire and patience. Summary answer and next steps below.

Summary (short):
- Backup/snapshot retention: Redwood's default production snapshot retention is 45 days; we hold snapshots in a 7-day soft window before physical purge. Upon purge we can provide a signed manifest of snapshot IDs with SHA-256 hashes plus a purge certificate showing purge job id and timestamp.
- Log retention exception: We can support a scoped 90-day retention for diagnostic logs on specified namespaces. This requires a signed change order (DocuSign link below), and will be subject to an incremental fee and quarterly attestation from Redwood's security team.

Actions for Mediconnect:
1) Please review and, if acceptable, sign the change order here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcdef-erase-agreement
2) Return the completed questionnaire (attached) so we can align on which namespaces need the extended logging.

Internal next steps (cc'd): Kimberly will provide the fee estimate and subprocessor notice; Rishi and Security will produce the attestation package quarterly once the exception is executed.

If you'd like a quick call to walk through the artifacts (purge manifest format, certificate fields), I'm happy to schedule one this week.

Best,
